title: TV Advertising and Online Sales: A Case Study of Intertemporal Substitution Effects for an Online Travel Platform
eligible_reason: Single-start field test: 11 treated counties begin a TV campaign simultaneously (15-day campaign after four weeks without TV ads), against 115 control counties, analyzed with synthetic difference-in-differences. One adoption date, and the estimator is synthetic DiD or an event study around individual ad airings (minute level).
design_notes: Main estimates use SDID with county, date and hour-of-day fixed effects weighted by SDID unit and time weights (Table 4, ln(Sessions+1) and ln(Sales+1) at 2-60 minute windows, SEs clustered by county; Figure 3 shows day-level trends). Table 3 is an event study around individual TV ad incidences in treated counties (30-minute windows, 24-hour attribution). Distributed-lag SDID models estimate intertemporal substitution. Six weeks of data in 2015 from one online travel agency in one country.
screener_notes: No replication package or regressions file was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only. Clickstream and TV ad schedule data are provided by the cooperating firm and the TV network (text near line 268). Not eligible: one adoption date and synthetic DiD.
